summary: An Indologist, Gaspare Gorresio studied at the Diocesan Seminary of Mondovì, the University of Turin under Amedeo Peyron, the University of Vienna, and with Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He held posts at the University of Turin, including the Sanskrit chair in 1852.

An Indologist, Gaston Courtillier studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 1897 under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot. He served as a professor at the Lycée de Mulhouse and Lycée Fustel de Coulanges, and taught Sanskrit at the University of Strasbourg from 1924.

Linguist Gaston Paris studied under Friedrich Christian Diez around 1856–1858 and at the École des chartes around 1858–1862. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1869 to 1903 and the Collège de France from 1872 to 1903.
Gaston Renondeau worked in the fields of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Polytechnique around 1899–1901.
A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gaton Ngawang Lekpa studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Gauri Viswanathan, working in Indology and other fields, studied at the University of Delhi and Columbia University (Ph.D. circa 1979–1985). She taught English at Delhi and became Professor in the Humanities and South Asia Institute Director at Columbia around 1989.

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Gaurinath Sastri served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (~1954–1969), Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society (~1957–1962), and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1970–1974).
A scholar in Indology and history/archaeology, Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha studied at Elphinstone College around 1883–1885 and under Bhagwanlal Indraji around 1885–1888.
Gautam Vajracharya is an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. His posts include affiliations with Samshodhana Mandala (attested 1982) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1997).

A scholar of religious studies and philosophy, Gavin D'Costa studied at the University of Cambridge and at the University of Birmingham under John Hick. He taught at West London Institute of Higher Education and held a post at the University of Bristol from 1993.

Indologist and religious studies scholar Gavin Flood studied at Lancaster University (~1976–1988) under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held posts at Lampeter (~1989–1998), Stirling (~1998–2005), and the University of Oxford and Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies (2005–2015).

Working in Indology and religious studies, Gaya Charan Tripathi studied under Ulrich Schneider around 1962–1966. He served as Principal of the Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha from circa 1977 to 1997.
An Indologist, Geetha K. Wilson is a doctoral student at the University of Tübingen under Claire Maes and holds a faculty post there (attested 2026).
Geir Heierstad works in Indology and other fields. He served as Director at Oslo Metropolitan University in 2014 and is attested as faculty at the University of Oslo in 2026.

A Tibetologist, Gelek has served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998), a visiting lecturer at the University of California, and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, Gelek Rimpoche studied at Drepung Monastery, Young Lamas Home School (~1960–1963), and Cornell University (1964). He directed Tibet House, New Delhi (1965) and founded Jewel Heart in 1988.

Gembo Dorji works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, as well as under traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki, an Indologist and historian, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1991). He was a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (~1961–1974) and held a professorial post at Kokugakuin University in 2006.
A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gendun Chopel studied at Drisha, Kumbum, Labrang, and Drepung Monasteries, learning under Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso.
A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gendun Chophel studied under Sherab Gyatso around 1921–1927 and held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.
